hypotheses.binder: (hw : ∀ n x, x ∈ s.domain → 0 ≤ w n x)
hypotheses.justification: `LocalJets` (PeriodizedWaveBounds.lean:52) requires, for every m, constants C ≥ 0 and p with ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ j (f n i) x‖ ≤ majorant s w α C p n x for all x ∈ s.domain ∩ K n i and all j ≤ m. Here `majorant s w α C p n x = C * ε^α * growth^p * w n x`. In the proof of `LocalJets.bilinear`, `hw` is used only once: in `majorant_nonneg s w α hA p n x (hw n x hx)`, which gives `0 ≤ majorant s w α A p n x` at a point x ∈ s.domain ∩ K n i. That fact already follows from `hf`: take j = 0 (and 0 ≤ m), so `0 ≤ ‖f n i x‖ ≤ majorant s w α A p n x`, i.e. `(norm_nonneg _).trans (ha n i x hx hi 0 (Nat.zero_le m))`. The rest of the proof is unchanged: the Leibniz bound from `bilinear_jet_at` / `JetBounds.norm_iteratedFDeriv_bilinear_le_on` (a public theorem), then `majorant_mul`, which has no sign condition. So the same argument, with L = `lsmul ℝ ℝ`, proves the statement without `hw`. Degenerate cases: if w is negative at some point of s.domain ∩ K n i, the bound at that point forces every C_m to be 0. The argument above still applies, because it only needs the majorant to be nonnegative at the points where it is used, and the j = 0 bound gives that. You cannot call `LocalJets.bilinear` as stated without `hw`, so the proof has to repeat its short argument with this one change. `hv` can be dropped the same way, and both can be dropped together.

hypotheses.binder: (hv : ∀ n x, x ∈ s.domain → 0 ≤ v n x)
hypotheses.justification: This is symmetric to `hw`. In the proof of `LocalJets.bilinear`, `hv` is used only to get `majorant_nonneg s v β hB q n x (hv n x hx)` at points x ∈ s.domain ∩ K n i. That nonnegativity follows from `hg` itself: the j = 0 bound gives `0 ≤ ‖g n i x‖ ≤ majorant s v β B q n x`, i.e. `(norm_nonneg _).trans (hb n i x hx hi 0 (Nat.zero_le m))`. The Leibniz estimate (`JetBounds.norm_iteratedFDeriv_bilinear_le_on`, public) and `majorant_mul` (no sign condition) then finish the proof exactly as before. So the theorem stays true and provable without `hv`, and also with both `hw` and `hv` removed.
